Fixes: Saving a very large file (350 MB or more) whose inside is laid out in an unusual way could give a file that would not open again. Files saved from now on open normally.

When the automatic recovery copy could not be written (disk full, or its folder busy), it is now tried again a little later, not only after your next change. And a tab brought back from the Start screen no longer deletes its earlier recovery copy before the new one is safely written.
Choosing Save in the "Save changes?" question while that file was still being saved did nothing, and the tab stayed open. It now waits for that save, then finishes.
Print › Save as PDF could replace the open PDF itself with its print version. It now asks for another name.
Export to Excel: bills of quantities whose headings differ only in their number (BILL No. 4 and BILL No. 5) were put on one sheet. Each now gets its own. Scanned pages are not changed by this fix.

Link the sheets: callouts near the right or bottom edge of a sheet are now linked (only the title block itself is skipped), and a small set (up to 9 sheets) where two sheets carry the same number is linked again, to the first of the two, with a note naming the number. Clicking a sheet link now shows the whole sheet, not its top-left corner.
Problem reports never reached the developer: the app sent them to the wrong address, and they were refused. They now arrive.

What you type in Report a problem now has paths, file names and web links taken out before it is sent, where the app can recognise them; the rest is sent as typed. Before, only your user name and PC name were taken out. (Earlier reports were refused by the server, so the developer never received them.)
The START HERE file in the test copy now says what the app sends over the internet.

New features: AI assistant: DeepSeek is a third choice next to Claude and ChatGPT, for questions about a file and for translation. Add your own DeepSeek key under AI keys; DeepSeek bills your own account.

What you send to DeepSeek goes to its servers (in China, by DeepSeek's privacy policy). Most of its models read text only: with one of those, only the text of the pages is sent, and the panel says so. To send drawings or scans, choose its model that reads pictures.
General polishing: On the heaviest sheets, saving after redactions or text edits is much faster and takes less memory. On a 5-million-line sheet it took under a second and a half in testing (over 11 seconds before), with about a third less memory.
Fixes: Undo after a redaction or a text edit on a sheet of millions of lines no longer ends in an error. The same goes for a sheet you had simplified.

Several redactions or text edits in a row on such a sheet could run out of memory: on a 5-million-line sheet the third one failed in testing, and Save and the automatic recovery copy failed with it. All three now work; four redactions in a row were applied and saved.

Save could fail with "compression bomb detected" after a redaction or text edit on a sheet of about 3 million lines or more, or in a file that holds one page or picture of over 100 MB. It was rare, because it depended on the exact size, but it goes back to version 0.10. When it happened nothing was written: the file on disk stayed as it was, and no file was damaged; what was at risk was the work not yet saved. These files now save.
Files over 350 MB: after a redaction or text edit on a heavy sheet, Save wrote that sheet unpacked, so the file came out bigger than needed. It is now packed.
An insert refused for lack of memory now says so, and what to do, instead of pointing at "too many links and markups".

New features: Lines and arrows: each end now has its own arrowhead setting, so an arrow can point both ways, or carry a different head at each end. A button swaps the two ends.
Spelling: right-click a word underlined in red in a text box or comment for suggestions and "Add to dictionary". The same menu has Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all.
Excel export of counts and measurements: a new "By sheet" sheet shows each item against each drawing sheet, with totals. Only sheets that carry marks are listed.

Link the sheets finds more drawing sets: large drawings whose number box also holds numbers that repeat from sheet to sheet are now recognised. In such sets a reference is linked only where it clearly points to one sheet; the others are left alone.
Link the sheets: the "Sheets" bookmarks now carry each sheet's title next to its number.
General polishing: Combine, Extract, Insert and printing of big sets need far less memory. A 300-sheet set with 300,000 links took about a seventh of the memory to combine in testing.
Inserting a big set is much faster: 1,500 sheets with 60,000 links went in in under 4 seconds in testing (79 seconds before). One Undo still removes them all.
Stop during Combine now stops at once and leaves nothing behind.
Printing a big file can be cancelled while it is prepared. A cancelled print says "The print was stopped."
Deleting or flattening many markups at once, and numbering the pages of a long file, are several times faster. Flattening 1,500 markups took under a second in testing (11 seconds before).
A sheet of millions of lines is prepared about twice as fast. It also keeps its fast drawing after page numbers or redaction are added to it, or after it is inserted into another file.

If part of the app stops answering, a notice asks: "Keep waiting" or "Restart it". If it is running out of memory, the app asks before it restarts; your changes are kept, but Undo starts again from there.
Mark, flatten and repair in Batch now work on very big files (over 1 GB) that used to fail.
Fixes: Link the sheets no longer takes numbers on bill of quantities pages for sheet numbers, so no links point to them.
A save that would pass 4 GB is refused with a plain message that suggests splitting the file. The file on disk is left as it was.
Protected or signed files over about 1.2 GB: the app says on opening that such a file cannot be saved here. Markups, printing and extracting pages still work.
Pictures to PDF: more than about 1 GB of pictures is refused before it starts, with the advice to make two or more PDFs and merge them.
A print too big to prepare gets a message asking you to print it in parts, instead of an error.

Combining no longer runs out of memory when one of the files holds a very large number of links or markups (hundreds of thousands, as some big drawing sets do). Such a combine used to fail; it now finishes.

New features: Link the sheets (Edit tab): reads each sheet's number and title from its title block, links every "see A-301" or detail reference to that sheet, and adds a "Sheets" bookmark group. Your own bookmarks are kept. One Undo removes it all; running it again replaces it. A 320-sheet set took about 1 second in testing; a combined set of 2,000 pages, 16 to 20 seconds.
Layers: a Layers panel turns a file's CAD layers on and off on screen, in print, in Save as PDF and in picture export. The file changes only when you press "Save the layer state".
Files up to 4 GB now open (the limit was 2 GB). Combining a big set gives a file you can open and work on: 40 files, 2.7 GB, were combined and opened in about 15 seconds in testing.
Excel exports (Comments list and Measurements): a new "PDF page" column gives the real page number next to the page label, so each markup can be found in the PDF.
The app now counts its users, anonymously. It asks at first start; one click turns it off, then or later in Settings › Privacy. The README says exactly what is sent.
General polishing: Link the sheets on a specification, a scan or a mixed set (drawings combined with scans, for example): it links only the real sheets, or says none were found and changes nothing.
Link the sheets with "Links between sheets" unticked leaves the links from an earlier run in place.
Layers also switch on screen in protected files (password or restricted permissions).
Settings › Updates: "Restore default" puts the update address back as the setup chose it, if it was changed or deleted by accident.
Fixes: A file that can no longer be read from its disk (moved, deleted, network gone) now gets a message saying so, instead of a crash report.
After "Save as" on a big combined file, the app no longer says later that the file cannot be read.
Background errors no longer raise crash reports.
Damaged files: errors from the editing engine no longer build up (it used to restart itself after many of them).
After deleting or extracting pages, the pages that are gone no longer cause errors.
A jump made right after "Fit page" (to a bookmark, for example) now lands on its page.

New features: A file with a sheet of millions of lines (traced from CAD) opens in a fraction of a second instead of 8–9 seconds. The sheet is prepared when you reach it ("Preparing this drawing…") and takes about as long to draw as before.
While a big file is saving, pages you haven't seen yet appear at once instead of after the save.
General polishing: The heaviest sheets need less than a third of the memory to draw (the heaviest one we test: 7.8 → about 2.3 GB), so they open on PCs with little memory to spare.
Selecting text and snapping answer at once while a heavy sheet is still drawing (they waited up to 2 seconds).
A drawing set with a very dense sheet scrolls about 30% faster, at a price: it can hold over 1 GB more memory while it is open.
Zooming far into a scanned page is faster when the PC has memory to spare (8×: 4.6 → 3.0 seconds).
Snapping is ready much sooner on dense drawings, and gives up at once on pages too dense to snap.
Zooming quickly through several levels: the levels you have already left are skipped.
Fixes: Closing a file gives back the memory it held; no temporary files are left behind after a save; a recovery copy can no longer be left half-written.

New features: Linux: Greenline PDF Editor now runs on Linux Mint, Ubuntu, Debian and similar - as an AppImage (one file, runs on most distributions) or a .deb package; both update themselves like the Windows version
Linux: Settings > "Make it the default for PDFs"; printing starts on the system's default printer
Number size is now a slider (Measure > Labels, 25% to 400%): nothing selected - every measurement number in the file; measurements selected - only those, bigger or smaller from their own size
Snapshot keeps its area marked: right-click it to print just that part (enlarged to the paper), copy it or save it as a picture; Esc or a click outside it unmarks it, as with a selection

General polishing: Pages already drawn no longer stay blank after Windows was locked or asleep: they are drawn again when you unlock or wake the PC, or when the graphics card's memory is reset (the app kept reusing the wiped pictures - pages seen before showed white until the file was opened again)

New features: Drawing engines can now use up to 4 GB each (2 GB before): a page whose pictures need more than 2 GB is drawn instead of stopping the engine. An engine still starts afresh quietly before that, at a point set by the PC's memory and the number of engines
Updates now list what every version you skipped brought - in the update card and in "Updated to" afterwards - not only the newest (going from 0.9.4 straight to 0.9.6 left out 0.9.5's fixes)
General polishing: A file whose index merely points a little off (common in PDFs saved from Excel) opens without the "was damaged" notice - repaired quietly, as Acrobat does. The notice stays for files really missing something: cut short (also within a section saved later), a page that can't be found, or a page's content, pictures, fonts or markups missing
Ortho (F8) now also straightens Length, Calibrate, Line and Arrow; a point that snapped to something stays on it with Ortho on (it was moved off its target)
Continue from this corner works with Area / Perimeter in rectangle or circle mode (it made a stray rectangle instead); the tip and the drawing bar count the rest of the shape while you continue
Snapping no longer misses the spot the pointer stops on while the drawing engine is busy

The magnifier follows the page when it scrolls or zooms under a still pointer, opens where the pointer is, and skips pages too heavy to draw sharp; the perpendicular snap only offers edges that are drawn
Make files searchable (several files): a drawing engine starting afresh during the run no longer fails the file

New features: ⊥ snapping: while you draw, a line near the pointer offers the point square to it from the point you came from - on the drawing's lines and on markup edges (as in the Estimation app)
Ortho (F8): lines and corners go straight - 0, 45 or 90° - without holding Shift
Crosshair (F6): lines across the view through the pointer, to line points up
Magnifier (F7): a loupe beside the pointer shows the exact point a click puts down, magnified 2 to 8 times
Continue from this corner: right-click any corner of an outline, or one in the middle of a line, and draw on from it - the rest of the shape stays
General polishing: The tip beside the pointer says what it snapped to while you draw
Coming next: Drawing engines that can use up to 4 GB each (2 GB now), for the very largest scans

General polishing: Big scanned files no longer stop a drawing engine in the middle of drawing: decoded scans are let go by the memory they take, and an engine that has grown big starts afresh quietly before it runs out
A drawing engine left idle with a lot of memory gives it back to Windows (a PC with several big scans open was left short of memory, and everything slowed down)
The engines start a little faster (one part was read twice at every start)
Anonymous problem reports: long file names in the log are now taken out whole (some got through), and dates are no longer blanked out
Coming next: Drawing engines that can use up to 4 GB each (2 GB now), for the very largest scans

General polishing: Stays quick as your stamps and signatures add up: the settings (which hold them) were read again from disk at nearly every step - opening a file, saving, every check
The store of page previews no longer slows the app down once it has filled up after months of use (it was looked through whole after every 60 pictures)
A style changed with a slider (opacity) is saved once you stop, not at every step
The Greenline name's green fades into the background at its end - in the title bar, on the start page and in the setup
The setup shows its full name and green too - its wordmark and buttons were still gold

Running the setup from a folder that also holds a copy of the release no longer makes that folder the place updates come from; the setup's Options and Settings › Updates have a one-click way back to the download page

New features: Report a problem no longer needs a GitHub account: your words (and the picture of the window, if you keep it) go to the developer anonymously - no name, no PC name, no file names, never your PDF files
Anonymous crash reports, off until you turn them on in Settings › Help - which also lists exactly what is sent, with an example
General polishing: Shows its full name - Greenline PDF Editor - in the title bar, taskbar, Start menu, Windows' list of apps and the setup, with its own green
The setup fills in where new versions come from by itself (this page); a shortcut left from 0.9.1 under the old name is removed
The Settings button is a cog you can recognise (it looked like a sun)

New features: Updates can also come from a web address - the public download page on GitHub - with the same signature and checksum checks; there, Report a problem opens a GitHub issue with your text
General polishing: Built-in browser (Electron) brought to 44.10.2 with its security fixes - this version installs with its setup (run it once on each PC)
Fixes: Print: a paper picked in the panel (A3, A2...) is now the paper the printer uses - A3 came out on A4 with only part of the drawing
Print: "Printer preferences..." opens the settings of the printer picked in the panel, not those of Windows' default printer
Count: Backspace pressed right after quick clicks took back the mark before the last one

General polishing: Built-in browser (Electron) brought to 44.10.2 with its security fixes - this version installs with its setup (run it once on each PC)
Fixes: Print: a paper picked in the panel (A3, A2...) is now the paper the printer uses - A3 came out on A4 with only part of the drawing
Print: "Printer preferences..." opens the settings of the printer picked in the panel, not those of Windows' default printer
Count: Backspace pressed right after quick clicks took back the mark before the last one

New features: Area gives the perimeter too (one tool instead of Area + Perimeter); Totals and To Excel list the perimeters apart

Drawing by points: Ctrl+Z / Backspace take back the last point, Ctrl+Y puts it back; Esc cancels and Ctrl+Z brings the shape back; Shift+C closes it; a bar at the foot of the page shows the length / area so far
Corners: drag the middle dot of an edge to add one, Alt+click (or right-click) to delete one; right-click > Continue this line
General polishing: A corner you drag snaps to line work, other markups and the shape's own corners (Shift: straight edge); a click on a corner no longer counts as an edit
Dialogs can be dragged by their title; Calibrate keeps the drawing visible behind it
Count: Backspace takes back the last mark; the tip shows each segment's direction
Fixes: Ctrl+Z while drawing an area or a line took back the markup made before instead of the last point

New features: Text boxes, callouts and typewriter text: bold, italic, underline, colour, size and font for the selected words only, like a word processor (Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I / Ctrl+U too) - with nothing selected the whole box changes, as before
General polishing: The formatting is saved the standard way, so other PDF programs show it and keep it; Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y while typing take back a style as well as typing
Bold or coloured words in comments made in other PDF programs stay that way when you edit them here

Fixes: Updates no longer stop with "didn't finish" when PDF Editor takes a moment to close: the update waits for it (takes effect once this version's setup has been run on the PC)
Explorer > Combine with PDF Editor works with many files at once (dozens of large drawings): the Merge window opens - it sometimes never came
Print offers Windows' default printer at every start (it could offer the first printer of the list, or the one used last time); a printer you pick is kept until PDF Editor is closed
General polishing: Files sent with Combine while another window is open (Settings, a password) say so, and open in Merge when it closes

New features: Area and Perimeter draw as corners, a rectangle or a circle (strip at the foot of the page, keys P / R / O); circles measure exactly
Type a length while measuring (4200, 4.2 m) and press Enter: the next point goes that far towards the mouse
Counts & totals panel (Measure > Totals): every count and the measurements added up, by name and page - no Excel needed
Count by tag (Measure > By tag…): door tags such as D01, D02 found on the drawing and counted in one go
Print: Send as Auto / As they are / Pictures - heavy scans and dense drawings go as one picture per sheet, a far lighter job for the printer
General polishing: A rectangle measurement keeps its square corners when a corner is dragged (Alt: the corner alone); a circle has one handle for its size
The print panel counts the seconds while the printer takes the job
Tabs of drawings from one set show the part of the name that differs; the left panel can't push the page out of view
The text box bar fits narrow windows and sits clear of a turned text box; Black & white shows in the print preview
The page box understands page labels (iii, A-2); Undo while typing in a new text box removes the box
Fixes: Switching tabs keeps each file where you left it - it used to jump to the top of page 1, sometimes zoomed into its left side
Text box bar: the font and size lists open again
Measurements pasted, duplicated or moved to another page, file or viewport show the number for their new place, and a later scale change updates them (some kept their old number)
Count numbers carry on after the highest one - deleting #2 no longer gives a second #3
Pages extracted, inserted or merged keep their scale; a viewport follows its page when the page is turned
A pencil stroke is kept when you press Escape, pick another tool or save straight after it
Number boxes (copies, scale %, header size...) can be emptied and typed over
Markups on a layer that is turned off are not printed or made visible by Flatten
Files of 2 GB or more: said plainly (they can't be opened here); a merge that big is kept where you choose
Square feet worked out exactly; an area whose sides cross is pointed out

New features: Rectangle area (Measure tab): drag from corner to corner, or click the two corners; Shift for a square
General polishing: Measurements to Excel: the number in its own column as a real number, the unit in the next column, the drawing's label beside them
Updates install without the antivirus stopping them (0.8.2's update was blocked on some PCs)
A future version that needs its setup says so - PDF Editor never starts a downloaded setup by itself
Fixes: Everything from 0.8.2 (search all open files, insert and replace pages, bookmarks, links, pictures, table area to Excel) is in this version

New features: Search all open files at once: results grouped by file, a click opens the right tab
Insert pages from another open tab, and Replace pages with revised sheets (bookmarks and links kept)
Bookmarks you can add, rename, move and delete
Table area to Excel: drag a box around a table on a drawing, only that goes to Excel
Save pages as pictures (PNG/JPG), and a new PDF from pictures or scans
Links: make, change and delete them; a web link always asks before it opens
Comments list to a PDF summary, with a picture of each markup
General polishing: Extract pages: type the pages like in Print, remove them from the original, save or open as a tab
The Pages panel keeps its place for each tab
Merging a very big set works, with progress and Stop
Large page inserts are many times faster; long sessions stay quick to mark up
Fixes: Deleting or moving pages no longer loses the file's form fields or measurement scales
Excel export of steel section tables (decimal commas, split columns)
Updates are checked for a valid signature before they are installed
A link to another file no longer jumps to a page of this one

General polishing: Ribbon pop-ups (colours, Tool Chest, Flatten) open in full, no longer cut off
OCR: one run is one undo step; Redo leaves pages with real text alone
AI: Stop works at any moment; a mistyped new key keeps the old one; translations carry on after a failure
The same file by another name (mapped drive or network path) goes to its open tab
Fixes: Remove password: the password no longer comes back at the next save
Text and page numbers added after OCR show on the page
Merge, Split and Extract keep markups, form fields and links
Digitally signed files: asked before a save that would break the signature
Print: the printer list was empty
A damaged settings file can no longer wipe your settings
Batch jobs never write over a file that is open

New features: Export to Word and Excel (File tab): tables, numbers as numbers, one sheet per bill
Scans exported too: read with OCR, stamps and coloured ink left out
Tabs: drag to reorder, drag out to a window of its own, drag back to join
Many files open: tabs shrink to fit; the list button shows them all
General polishing: Bills over many pages join into one sheet, header once
Word: headings, lists, page numbers, headers and footers kept
Fixes: OCR'd scans: text selection and highlights sit on the words, not above them

New features: Stamp from a scan or photo: background removed, straightened, real size
Copy a stamp to all pages (same corner on every sheet size)
Stamp from a page: box a stamp on a scanned page
General polishing: Signatures from a scan cleaned the same way
Stamps keep their shape when resized (Shift to stretch)
Messages show above open dialogs; names under Your stamps
Fixes: Picture stamps no longer squash when resized
Picture stamps upright on turned pages
Callouts on pages turned 270° keep their pointer

General polishing: Measurement numbers a bit bigger; Ctrl+Z right after a ribbon list or box
Fixes: Measurement arrows sized to the number, not huge
Selected shapes: colour, width and ends from the ribbon
Antivirus blocking an update: the app stays open and points to the setup

New features: Combine PDFs from Explorer: select, right-click > Combine with PDF Editor
Measurements: decimals and unit, before or after measuring (m: 3, mm: 0)
Measurement numbers: one size for the whole file, sized to your zoom
Separate X and Y scales for stretched drawings and sections
What's new: File tab, any time
General polishing: Text cursor over text when highlighting
Decimals (m) on the Measure ribbon
Clear messages: file open in Excel, folder gone, files that can't be merged
Fixes: Very heavy drawings now open
Other programs' text boxes no longer garble when rotated
Setup no longer stuck on a green screen
Fewer false crash reports; a page too heavy to draw says so

0.5.0: Arabic in text boxes, callouts, typewriter and edited page text - joined letters, right to left, searchable
Fonts from this PC for markups and text (Calibri, Times, Arial, Tahoma...), bold and italic - included in the saved file
Report a problem (File tab); crashes are noted by themselves
Many fixes: counts numbered right, review status kept, cut and paste of markups, edits made while saving, password-protected files, printing of hidden layers and replies
0.4.0: One-file installer: just you (no admin) or everyone on the PC, shortcuts, Open with
Updates from the company's shared folder - asks before downloading, quiet away from the office
